body.x: ILias AI Co., Ltd. (CEO Ko Bumsuk) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the Incheon IFEZ Pavilion. The company specializes in developing scent intelligence technology that digitizes smells into data. Since its founding in 2022, it has aimed to commercialize olfactory-based products and service platforms across various industries.

At CES 2025, ILias AI introduced its flagship product, the Digital Sniffer Dog, designed for use in airports and seaports. This innovative scanner captures and analyzes odors from passengers and luggage to detect illegal drugs. Using a multi-channel sensor array and AI-driven scent intelligence, the device mimics human olfactory receptors to identify specific airborne odors.

The embedded AI system leverages pre-trained drug scent data for accurate and reliable detections. Unlike traditional visual, chemical, or physical drug detection methods, the Digital Sniffer Dog digitizes odors and processes multidimensional data for precision. This reduces the discomfort associated with physical inspections, provides rapid screenings, and enables the detection of new and evolving drug types through continuous deep-learning updates.

body.cap: ILias AI’s Director Mark Junggook Seo (left) explaining the Digital Sniffer Dog to AVING News reporter Alex Sigrist at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The system supports 24/7 automated operation, enabling large-scale screenings with higher sensitivity than X-ray scanners or ion detectors. It offers consistent detection performance while significantly reducing training costs and maintaining live sniffer dogs.

ILias AI emphasized, “Our Digital Sniffer Dog revolutionizes traditional drug detection methods, offering exceptional value in large-scale security environments like airports and seaports. The AI-driven olfactory technology ensures fast and accurate detection, enhancing operational efficiency and security reliability.”

The company further explained its strategic goals: “Participating in CES 2025 allows us to demonstrate our advanced technology globally, particularly as we aim to establish a U.S. branch by mid-2025. This event is a key platform for networking with U.S. Homeland Security, international security firms, and potential investors.”

body.cap: CES 2025 attendees learning about ILias AI’s Digital Sniffer Dog at their booth. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Through this groundbreaking technology, ILias AI aims to redefine the standards of drug detection systems, contributing to more effective and efficient security solutions worldwide.
AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
